stanzas.sanskrit:
सत्राजितस्त्वमथ लुब्धवदर्कलब्धं
दिव्यं स्यमन्तकमणिं भगवन्नयाचीः ।
तत्कारणं बहुविधं मम भाति नूनं
तस्यात्मजां त्वयि रतां छलतो विवोढुम् ॥ ८०-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Satraajit, a yadhava, prayed to Sun-god and got Syamantaka Mani, a priceless jewel as gift. Krishna asked Satraajit to give that jewel. Reasons for asking could have been many, but one main reason could be the strategy to marry his daughter Sathyabhama, who was in love with Krishna.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
satrājitastvamatha lubdhavadarkalabdhaṃ
divyaṃ syamantakamaṇiṃ bhagavannayācīḥ |
tatkāraṇaṃ bahuvidhaṃ mama bhāti nūnaṃ
tasyātmajāṃ tvayi ratāṃ chalato vivoḍhum || 80-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अदत्तं तं तुभ्यं मणिवरमनेनाल्पमनसा
प्रसेनस्तद्भ्राता गलभुवि वहन् प्राप मृगयाम् ।
अहन्नेनं सिंहो मणिमहसि मांसभ्रमवशात्
कपीन्द्रस्तं हत्वा मणिमपि च बालाय ददिवान् ॥ ८०-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Narrow minded Satraajit did not give it to Krishna, instead gave it to his brother Prasena. When he wore it around his neck and went for hunting, a lion thinking the jewel is flesh, attacked and killed him and took it. Jaambavaan, King of all animals, killed the lion and took the jewel and gifted it to his child.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
adattaṃ taṃ tubhyaṃ maṇivaramanenālpamanasā
prasenastadbhrātā galabhuvi vahan prāpa mṛgayām |
ahannenaṃ siṃho maṇimahasi māṃsabhramavaśāt
kapīndrastaṃ hatvā maṇimapi ca bālāya dadivān || 80-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शशंसुः सत्राजिद्गिरमनु जनास्त्वां मणिहरं
जनानां पीयूषं भवति गुणिनां दोषकणिका ।
ततः सर्वज्ञोऽपि स्वजनसहितो मार्गणपरः
प्रसेनं तं दृष्ट्वा हरिमपि गतोऽभूः कपिगुहाम् ॥ ८०-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Satraajit announced that Krishna has stolen the jewel and people believed it too. A small fault in conduct, if found in good people, everyone will keep talking about it with great interest. Krishna knew everything that has happened to the jewel but still HE went in search of it. HE came across Prasena & the lion lying dead & were led to Jaambavaan’s cave.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śaśaṃsuḥ satrājidgiramanu janāstvāṃ maṇiharaṃ
janānāṃ pīyūṣaṃ bhavati guṇināṃ doṣakaṇikā |
tataḥ sarvajño’pi svajanasahito mārgaṇaparaḥ
prasenaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā harimapi gato’bhūḥ kapiguhām || 80-3 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भवन्तमवितर्कयन्नतिवयाः स्वयं जाम्बवान्
मुकुन्दशरणं हि मां क इह रोद्धुमित्यालपन् ।
विभो रघुपते हरे जय जयेत्यलं मुष्टिभि-
-श्चिरं तव समर्चनं व्यधित भक्तचूडामणिः ॥ ८०-४ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Due to old age, Jaambavaan failed to recognise Krishna and exclaimed that no one can win him, who has Mukundan as the saviour. With prayers to Lord Ram, he did pooja for Krishna with the blow of fists for almost 21 days.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhavantamavitarkayannativayāḥ svayaṃ jāmbavān
mukundaśaraṇaṃ hi māṃ ka iha roddhumityālapan |
vibho raghupate hare jaya jayetyalaṃ muṣṭibhi-
-ściraṃ tava samarcanaṃ vyadhita bhaktacūḍāmaṇiḥ || 80-4 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
बुद्ध्वाऽथ तेन दत्तां
नवरमणीं वरमणिं च परिगृह्णन् ।
अनुगृह्णन्नमुमागाः
सपदि च सत्राजिते मणिं प्रादाः ॥ ८०-५ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Later Jaambavaan recognised that the person whom he fought with is Sri Krishna, he gave his beautiful daughter & Syamantaka mani to Krishna. Bhagwan accepted and immediately returned the jewel to Satraajit.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
buddhvā’tha tena dattāṃ
navaramaṇīṃ varamaṇiṃ ca parigṛhṇan |
anugṛhṇannamumāgāḥ
sapadi ca satrājite maṇiṃ prādāḥ || 80-5 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
तदनु स खलु व्रीडालोलो विलोलविलोचनां
दुहितरमहो धीमान् भामां गिरैव परार्पिताम् ।
अदितमणिना तुभ्यं लभ्यं समेत्य भवानपि
प्रमुदितमनास्तस्यैवादान्मणिं गहनाशयः ॥ ८०-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Satraajit felt ashamed that he had accused Krishna wrongly. He had only verbally promised that he will give his daughter in marriage to someone. But after this incident, he gave his beautiful eyed daughter Satyabhama & Syamantaka mani to Krishna. Having received the stree ratnam Sathyabhama itself, Krishna was happy and hence returned the jewel to Satraajit himself.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
tadanu sa khalu vrīḍālolo vilolavilocanāṃ
duhitaramaho dhīmān bhāmāṃ giraiva parārpitām |
aditamaṇinā tubhyaṃ labhyaṃ sametya bhavānapi
pramuditamanāstasyaivādānmaṇiṃ gahanāśayaḥ || 80-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
व्रीलाकुलां रमयति त्वयि सत्यभामां
कौन्तेयदाहकथयाथ कुरून् प्रयाते ।
ही गान्दिनेयकृतवर्मगिरा निपात्य
सत्राजितं शतधनुर्मणिमाजहार ॥ ८०-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna was having a delightful time with Satyabhama. News of Kunti's sons burnt in wax palace reached Krishna and HE immediately left to Hastinapur. With the promptings of Akrura and Kritivermaa, Shatadanva killed Satraajit and took away the Syamantaka mani.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
vrīlākulāṃ ramayati tvayi satyabhāmāṃ
kaunteyadāhakathayātha kurūn prayāte |
hī gāndineyakṛtavarmagirā nipātya
satrājitaṃ śatadhanurmaṇimājahāra || 80-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
शोकात्कुरूनुपगतामवलोक्य कान्तां
हत्वा द्रुतं शतधनुं समहर्षयस्ताम् ।
रत्ने सशङ्क इव मैथिलगेहमेत्य
रामो गदां समशिशिक्षत धार्तराष्ट्रम् ॥ ८०-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Hearing about the father's death, Satyabhama was struck with grief and she reached Hastinapur. Krishna immediately killed Shatadanva and pleased Satyabhama. Balaram went to Mithila and there, he trained Duryodhana in the art of wielding the mace.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
śokātkurūnupagatāmavalokya kāntāṃ
hatvā drutaṃ śatadhanuṃ samaharṣayastām |
ratne saśaṅka iva maithilagehametya
rāmo gadāṃ samaśiśikṣata dhārtarāṣṭram || 80-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अक्रूर एष भगवन् भवदिच्छयैव
सत्राजितः कुचरितस्य युयोज हिंसाम् ।
अक्रूरतो मणिमनाहृतवान् पुनस्त्वं
तस्यैव भूतिमुपधातुमिति ब्रुवन्ति ॥ ८०-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Akrurar, extremely devoted to Krishna, had prompted the killing of Satraajit, due to his love for Krishna in order to avenge for the blame, Satrajit put on Krishna initially. Krishna did not take the jewel from Akrurar but let him keep the jewel himself. Krishna wanted to bring prosperity to Akrura and hence did not recover the jewel and blessed him.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
akrūra eṣa bhagavan bhavadicchayaiva
satrājitaḥ kucaritasya yuyoja hiṃsām |
akrūrato maṇimanāhṛtavān punastvaṃ
tasyaiva bhūtimupadhātumiti bruvanti || 80-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भक्तस्त्वयि स्थिरतरः स हि गान्दिनेय-
-स्तस्यैव कापथमतिः कथमीश जाता ।
विज्ञानवान् प्रशमवानहमित्युदीर्णं
गर्वं ध्रुवं शमयितुं भवता कृतैव ॥ ८०-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Akrurar was humbled by the magnanimity shown by Krishna to him. How could there be an evil thought in his mind (of killing Satraajit and getting the jewel)? He was bloated with the vanity of having self knowledge and self control. Bhagwan brought this about in order to curb this.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhaktastvayi sthirataraḥ sa hi gāndineya-
-stasyaiva kāpathamatiḥ kathamīśa jātā |
vijñānavān praśamavānahamityudīrṇaṃ
garvaṃ dhruvaṃ śamayituṃ bhavatā kṛtaiva || 80-10 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
यातं भयेन कृतवर्मयुतं पुनस्त-
-माहूय तद्विनिहितं च मणिं प्रकाश्य ।
तत्रैव सुव्रतधरे विनिधाय तुष्यन्
भामाकुचान्तरशयः पवनेश पायाः ॥ ८०-११ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Still once again, Akrurar fled in fear along with Kritivermaa. Krishna brought Akrurar back along with the jewel and showed it to Balaram and others. Krishna gave the jewel to Akrurar, the one who does virtuous deeds.
Bhattathiri worshipped Bhagwan to protect him from his ailments.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
yātaṃ bhayena kṛtavarmayutaṃ punasta-
-māhūya tadvinihitaṃ ca maṇiṃ prakāśya |
tatraiva suvratadhare vinidhāya tuṣyan
bhāmākucāntaraśayaḥ pavaneśa pāyāḥ || 80-11 ||
